content.comment_body: I've recently built my first analog circuit and included a temperature sensor. My background is mainly with 24VAC [article_no], managing digital I/O. Can anyone recommend suitable components for this setup? Ideally, I'm looking for a [product_name] version, temperature sensor with 10-15m cable range, and appropriate power supply.

The 24V AC [product_name] doesn’t include built-in analog inputs, so you’ll need at least one analog expansion module. You haven’t specified if you only want a single temperature measurement or additional measurements. More details about your requirements would help.

The current setup uses one temperature sensor. There are 3 outputs that turn OFF as temperature increases: Q1 at 35F, Q2 at 25F, Q3 at 15F. The connected loads are 24V and 120V AC. Is it feasible to use an analog module with a 24V AC base unit? Would a 12/24V DC base and matching power supply be a more cost-effective choice?
Analog inputs and outputs typically work only with devices powered by DC supplies. There are no analog expansion modules designed for use with AC-powered units.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing the technical requirements and hardware compatibility for analog temperature measurements in a PLC setup. They are primarily trying to clarify the relationship between the base unit's power supply type (AC vs. DC) and analog expansion module support, with questions about practicality and cost-effectiveness.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect clear guidance on selecting hardware that is both compatible and cost-effective for analog temperature measurement, focusing on expansion module requirements and suitable base units.
